pre-market brief. Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

VERIFIED TAPE (from exchange OHLC data; authoritative, do not restate different prices):
| Ticker | Company | Cap | Screen | 1D close | 5D | Vol× 10d | Vol/gap event |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| DFH | Dream Finders Homes, Inc. | Small | Top 10 · 1D return · Mid & small cap | +12.07% | -11.4% | 3.0× | — |
| ZG | Zillow Group, Inc. Class A | Mid | Top 10 · 1D return · Mid & small cap | +11.70% | +8.1% | 1.1× | — |
| CRWV | CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock | Large | Vol spike / gapper · last 5D · Large cap | +4.59% | -15.4% | 4.4× | volume_spike 2026-10-15 |
| BSP | Bending Spoons S.p.A. | Large | Vol spike / gapper · last 5D · Large cap | +3.85% | +50.9% | 1.7× | both 2026-10-14 |

TASK
Run a separate search for EACH ticker ("<company> stock news", "<company> shares <session date>").
Find why it moved on Thursday October 15, 2026, any after-hours / pre-market move on Friday October 16, 2026, and
other material news in the window. Search press releases (BusinessWire, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire),
SEC filings, FDA, Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, Investor's Business Daily,
company IR pages, analyst-action roundups.
If a mover has no company news, check whether another company's event moved it (customer, supplier,
competitor, partner, sector report) and name that company and event.

OUTPUT (markdown; one section per ticker, in the order given; no intro or conclusion):

## Company Name (TICKER) `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or a concise sector name (Pharma, Energy, Retail, ...).
If you find nothing, write exactly one bullet: "- No company-specific catalyst found in window" and,
if applicable, a second bullet naming the sympathy driver.

Include when available: catalyst for the move, earnings figures, guidance, analyst actions, contracts
with $ size, filings, regulatory decisions, management quotes with numbers, next catalyst date.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Dream Finders Homes, Inc. (DFH) `[Homebuilding]`
- DFH shares rose 12.07% on October 15 after rebounding from a 20% drop on October 14 linked to speculation about an upcoming Bear Cave short report; no published Bear Cave report was identified in the window (Seeking Alpha, Oct 15 15:15 ET).[8]
- A company disclosure filed October 13 reported that DFH exercised an accordion provision on its revolving credit facility, increasing aggregate commitments by $220 million to approximately $1.7 billion; the filing was outside the window but was cited as background to the move (Seeking Alpha, Oct 15 15:15 ET).[8]

## Zillow Group, Inc. Class A (ZG) `[Internet & Platforms]`
- No company-specific catalyst found in window.

## CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock (CRWV) `[AI Infrastructure]`
- CoreWeave shares initially fell approximately 8% on October 15 before reversing higher; the session followed concerns about AI-infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, and a Gartner report warning that more than 80% of neocloud providers could fail to survive independently by 2030 (Investor’s Business Daily, Oct 15 13:41 ET).[1]
- D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria said CoreWeave could be the first casualty if the AI cycle faltered and assigned a zero-equity-value scenario; the comments were reported from a podcast and were marked [report] (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 08:28 ET).[3]
- Mizuho cut its CoreWeave price target to $88 from $115; Deutsche Bank maintained a Buy rating and a $150 price target, while Creditsights’ Paul Meeks called the selloff excessive (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 10:50 ET).[6]
- CoreWeave’s unsecured bonds due in 2032 traded below 80 cents on the dollar, while reported yields on its 2032 and 2031 bonds approached 14.8% and 14.9%, respectively (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 08:24 ET).[7]
- CoreWeave reported second-quarter revenue of approximately $2.58 billion, up 112.3% year over year, a $104 billion backlog, a $626 million net loss, $640 million of interest expense versus $267 million a year earlier, and $5.74 billion of negative free cash flow; the figures were previously disclosed and cited as background (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 15:19 ET).[4]
- CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator sold 78,552 Class A shares at $87.69 on September 30 for $6,888,224.88 under a 10b5-1 plan; the transaction was outside the window and was cited in same-day commentary (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 15:19 ET).[4]
- The next reported earnings date was expected around November 11, 2026 (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 08:24 ET).[9]

## Bending Spoons S.p.A. (BSP) `[Software & SaaS]`
- Berkshire Hathaway invested an additional $330 million in Bending Spoons, taking its ownership to approximately 4%; the transaction was announced October 15 and drove coverage of the shares (CNBC, Oct 15 06:57 ET).[2]
- Berkshire’s additional investment followed an approximately $600 million investment at Bending Spoons’ July 2026 IPO, bringing its total commitment to approximately $930 million (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 15:57 ET).[5]
- The additional shares were reportedly purchased in a private placement at $33 per share, approximately 13% below the prior day’s close and about 40% below the market price cited in the report; the pricing was marked [report] (Yahoo Finance, Oct 15 15:38 ET).[10]
